questions.stem: The CELLS responsible for producing antibodies are:
questions.explanation: B-lymphocytes → differentiate into plasma cells → secrete antibodies (immunoglobulins: IgG, IgM, IgA, IgE, IgD). T-lymphocytes (T-cells) handle cellular immunity (helper CD4, cytotoxic CD8). Both WBC types originate in bone marrow; T-cells mature in thymus, B-cells in bone marrow.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Edward Jenner developed the world's FIRST vaccine against:
questions.explanation: Edward Jenner (England, 1796) — used material from a cowpox sore on a milkmaid to inoculate 8-year-old James Phipps; boy later exposed to smallpox was unaffected. 'Vaccine' — from Latin 'vacca' (cow). Smallpox eradicated globally in 1980. Rabies vaccine — Louis Pasteur (1885). using cowpox material, 1796.
questions.subject: Biology

options.option_text: Immunity transferred from mother to child

questions.explanation: Active — body makes its own antibodies (from vaccine or natural infection); long-lasting but takes time to develop. Passive — ready-made antibodies transferred (mother-to-baby via placenta/milk, or antitoxin injection); immediate but short-term. COVID vaccines induce active immunity; monoclonal antibody drugs give passive. body produces antibodies itself.

_fixes.was: Immunity obtained by vaccine/infection; body produces antibodies itself

questions.stem: The universal BLOOD PLASMA donor is blood group:
questions.explanation: AB blood — no antibodies in plasma → universal PLASMA donor. But for RED CELL transfusions, AB is the universal RECIPIENT, and O-negative is the universal RBC DONOR. The two are different directions!. has no anti-A or anti-B antibodies in plasma.

questions.stem: The COVISHIELD vaccine (used widely in India's COVID-19 campaign) is manufactured by:
questions.explanation: Covishield — SII (Pune) licensed from Oxford University + AstraZeneca; viral vector (ChAdOx1) technology. Covaxin — Bharat Biotech (Hyderabad) + ICMR — inactivated whole-virus. ZyCoV-D — Zydus Cadila (first DNA vaccine approved in India, 2021). licensed Oxford-AstraZeneca formula.
questions.subject: Biology

_fixes.was: Serum Institute of India (SII) — licensed Oxford-AstraZeneca formula

questions.stem: The organ that is considered part of BOTH the IMMUNE and ENDOCRINE system, producing thymosin to mature T-cells, is:
questions.explanation: Thymus — located behind sternum, above heart. T-cells mature here (hence 'T' for thymus). Most active in childhood, shrinks with age. Produces thymosin. Spleen — largest lymphoid organ, filters blood. Pancreas — insulin (islet of Langerhans).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: AUTOIMMUNE diseases are conditions in which:

options.option_text: Immune system mistakenly attacks the body's own cells / tissues

questions.explanation: Autoimmune — the body's immune system fails to distinguish 'self' from 'non-self' and attacks own tissues. Examples: rheumatoid arthritis (joints), lupus (SLE, multiple organs), type 1 diabetes (pancreatic beta cells), multiple sclerosis (nerve myelin), Hashimoto's thyroiditis.
